text:
marta: noticing a perf regression on qwen2.5 after yesterday's autokernel tweak. latency p50 up ~18% for short-chat workloads and some KV hits look off. repro steps and quick numbers below. :frowning:

sam: ugh. which change exactly? commit hash?

marta: 6f3ae2b — change was: autokernel now prefers fused-softwindow kernel for seq<=64 unless detected mismatch. we flipped it to reduce p95 in large batches.

ida: I ran a tiny bisect, looks correlated with that flip. also saw weird kv cache dim mismatch in a multilingual tokenizer run (zh+en). sample logs:

```
[INFO] kv_cache: expected heads=32, kv_dim=128, got heads=40, kv_dim=160 on layer 10
[WARN] tokenizer: token boundary split: 3->4 tokens for `“你好world”`
Latency p50 (single-request): before 38ms -> after 45ms
```

kevin: interesting — heads mismatch implies we're feeding a model variant (40h/160kv) into kernel path expecting 32h/128kv. autokernel selection probably used a heuristic that maps model.name -> kernel profile, and the tokenizer split changed sequence length distribution, pushing scheduler into softwindow path.

ryan: can you push the profiler traces? I want flame graphs for the before/after to see kernel hotspots.

marta: attached quick pprof snapshot (trimmed):

```
pprof: total 1.2s samples
  40%  kernel_fused_softwindow
  30%  kv_cache_lookup
  15%  attention_kv_pack
  10%  tokenizer_normalize
  5%   other
```

marta: before the flip, kernel_autoselect used kernel_fused_baseline which showed: 55% baseline_compute, 20% kv_cache_lookup, 15% attention_kv_pack. so the softwindow kernel moves more work into kv lookup and pack.

ida: the multilingual tokenizer causing extra splits increases average sequence length for a short-chat workload (most English-only queries were <24 tokens, zh-mixed bumped to ~36). that can change batching heuristics and kernel choice. I think we have two separate factors: 1) tokenizer -> seqlen distribution 2) autokernel mapping that doesn't account for kv head dims correctly for Qwen variants.

kevin: quick reproduction command I used: `rti-bench --model qwen2.5 --prompt-file samples/mixed_zh_en.txt --profile --batching adaptive`

marta: confirmation: disabling autokernel flip (force baseline kernel) drops p50 back to 39ms and KV warnings disappear.

sam: ok plan: (1) revert flip on edge pool immediately for safety, (2) add stricter kernel compatibility check that validates head/kv dims from model metadata not heuristic name, (3) add tokenizer-aware sampling to our autokernel trainer so we include mixed-lang short-chat traces.

ryan: agree; also let's add a regression alert on p50 for seqlen<64 workloads so this doesn't slip.

runtime-profiling-bot: [auto] regression alert created: "qwen2.5 short-chat p50 delta > 15%" — alert-id: perf-1723456789. acknowledged.

marta: I'll open the revert PR now and attach repro script + reduced dataset. ping me if you want access to the trace VM. :thumbsup:

ida: once reverted I'll run a more exhaustive kernel selection sweep including ALiBi vs RoPE variants and KV head checks. I suspect RoPE scaling interactions yield different memory access patterns with softwindow kernels.

kevin: noted. I also want to add a runtime assert that refuses kernel selection if kv_dim/head count mismatches model.json declared values. low risk change.

sam: thanks all, good triage. keep thread updated when PR merges. :eyes:
